name: Prebuilt 0.945
commit_message:
Fix MIDI out dropping notes when playing from sequencer

Needed to buffer notes from the sequencer, they were coming quickly enough that they were overwriting the single note buffer previously used.
That was good enough for local playing, but having several notes firing at the same time would cause all but the last one to be overwritten, and so not sent.

name: Prebuilt 0.941
commit_message:
v0.941: New MENU 89 to work around sysex issue

Some computers (like Windows machines) cannot reliably receive USB sysex data sent at full speed.
Added MENU 89, which lets the user set how many milliseconds of delay are inserted between each 256 byte chunk of sysex data.
The code defaults it to 50ms, which gives reliable voice sample uploading on my Lenovo T14 running Windows 10.
I can get reliable sample uploading with it set to 0ms on my M1 MacBook Pro. That setting causes the Lenovo to corrupt some of the received sample data.
Also added length parameter to sample sysex messages so the luma tool can sanity check the received length.
Also bumped the version # to 0.941.

name: Prebuilt 0.940
commit_message:
Improved sysex sample transfers.

NOTE! Recommended toolchain is Arduino 1.8.19 + Teensy 1.58.
A known issue in the Arduino/Teensy toolchain and/or libraries can result in corruption when transferring large blocks of data over USB MIDI.
DIN5 MIDI appears to not have this issue (but is of course slower).
For more details, see:
https://forum.pjrc.com/index.php?threads/usbmidi-transmission-error.70288/

name: Prebuilt 0.938
commit_message:
Bug fixes, added way to play soft notes w/o MIDI velocity

fixed: DIN-5 OMNI mode not working. USB OMNI was OK.
fixed: restore Soft Thru setting at boot.
fixed: MENU 80 display problems for channels > 09
added: Parallel MIDI notes for soft sounds to enable triggering soft sounds w/o MIDI velocity. There is a parallel mapping of notes 2 octaves down which will trigger soft versions of corresponding sounds when available. For example, you can send a C1 with vel 127 or 63 to trigger the loud and soft BASS drum, respectively. With this new change, you can send C1 with vel 127 to trigger the loud BASS drum and now C-1 with vel 127 to trigger the soft BASS drum.
There is a new MENU 88 to select whether Luma sends velocity or sends these new note values for soft sounds.
There are only 5 sounds which have loud and soft sounds: BASS, SNARE, HIHAT, TAMB, and CABASA.

name: Prebuilt 0.936
commit_message:
Improved MIDI Clock sync

NOTE: Use this with MENU 87 (MIDI Start Enable) set to disabled!
You will need to manually arm Luma-1 before playing.
Set rear switch to MIDI CLOCK.
Select pattern you wish to play.
Hit PLAY/STOP, light will come on but it won't play yet.
Send MIDI Start and MIDI Clock, Luma-1 will start playing with tempo set by MIDI Clock tempo.

name: Prebuilt 0.928
commit_message:
MIDI Start/Stop changes

Hopefully fix the occasional crash when handling MIDI Start/Stop. I do 3 z-80 bus accesses, and was very briefly (~80ns) deasserting /BR between the first and second.
Hopefully fixed the occasional z-80 sequencer wedge when processing MIDI Stop. For MIDI Clock sources that are gated by MIDI Start/Stop (like Ableton Live), stopping the z-80 sequencer just as the clock was stopping would sometimes leave it in a bad state. Not crashed, just half-stopped. Now I always "skid" the MIDI clock to a stop by inserting a few fake tempo clock pulses after handling the MIDI Stop.
Finally, added a new front panel command to let the user toggle off/on whether Luma-1 honors MIDI Start/Stop. Tap MENU, then tap CHAIN ON/OFF. The state will toggle and you'll hear a beep. The current state is now shown on the main screen.

name: Prebuilt 0.927
commit_message:
Fix fan enable bug introduced with pop fix

Fan enable bits in same register as Beep bit, which was causing pop on MIDI drum trigger.
Properly save and restore state so I don't break fan enabling. :-)

name: Prebuilt 0.926
commit_message:
Fix intermittent pop on MIDI drum triggers

Honor the current state of the D802 control register, which controls drum trigger access and (among other things) the software Beep generator.

name: Prebuilt 0.925
commit_message:
More MIDI Start/Stop work

Now we check a variable in the Z-80 RAM to see if the sequencer is already running when we get a MIDI Start or already stopped when we get a MIDI Stop. And we only simulate the foot pedal press if we need to start/stop.

MIDI Start/Stop support

name: Prebuilt 0.922
commit_message:
MIDI Clock Fixes

Changed the way MIDI clock is converted into the Tempo Clock pulses for the Z-80.
Simpler approach than before. Verified with oscilloscope and by recording simple pattern into Ableton Live.
See LM_MIDI.ino for most of the changes.

name: Prebuilt 0.921
commit_message:
MIDI Clock Fixes

Some hardware sequencers send MIDI clock continuously.
Qualify MIDI clock with MIDI Start/Stop.
Some hardware sequencers send MIDI Continue instead of MIDI Start. Honor MIDI Continue as MIDI Start, at least for now. Eventually we should be able to restart the Luma-1 sequencer on MIDI Start.
